newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen futures end down but off lows.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen futures end down but off lows.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures ended Wednesday's TIFFE day session down but off their lows.
December settled at 99.11, after trading between 99.08 and 99.13. Turnover for the day session was 76,091 lots.
The key contract pared losses in the afternoon as Tokyo stocks extended losses. Japanese government bond futures' rebound from lows also provided support, traders said.
The Nikkei 225 stock average ended down 318.33 points, or 1.77 percent, at 17,703.37.
Meanwhile, key June JGB futures ended up 0.03 at 127.03 after falling as low as 126.61.
JGBs erased losses towards the end of the session following comments by Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka that Japan would maintain its current easy credit policy.
"Compared with JGB futures, euroyen futures' upside was heavy. Those players predicting the yield curve will continue to flatten may be selling for hedging purposes," said a city bank trader.
Euroyen futures opened lower in reaction to reported remarks by a key Finance Ministry official which suggested Japan's long-term interest rates could rise, traders said.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, was quoted by the Yomiuri Shimbun daily as saying that long-term interest rates were at record low levels, but could rise once people realise that the Japanese economy is not that bad.
Euroyen futures briefly pared part of their initial losses after the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) money market operation, which was more accommodative than expected.
The BOJ injected 100 billion yen into the money market, leaving a surplus of about 300 billion yen.
Market participants had expected the central bank to leave a surplus of about 100 billion yen by draining 100 billion yen today, traders said.
The unsecured overnight call rate was traded at 0.44 percent, down sharply from Tuesday's weighted average of 0.51 percent.
"As December euroyen futures have fallen below the 99.10 support point, they are likely to move between 99.05 and 99.15 in the near future," said the city bank trader.
Bidding activity on the payment side at the shorter-end of the yield curve in the interest rate swap (IRS) market was also weighing on euroyen futures, traders said.
About 260 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued at 0.55 percent. They were issued at 0.55 and 0.54 percent on Tuesday.
About 40 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.53 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
Two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent, unchanged from the previous session.
